summary: The chaos experiments confirmed that single‑replica services are vulnerable to outages and performance degradation. A pod failure in the frontend caused a critical site outage, while killing the cartservice led to a high‑severity error spike and service disruption. Redis‑cart pod termination produced a high‑latency slowdown but no data loss, highlighting the need for persistence and replication.

findings.title: Frontend pod failure caused site outage
findings.what_happened: The sole frontend pod crashed, making the service unhealthy and blocking all downstream traffic. Error rate spiked to 0.2045 and p95 latency reached 1100 ms during the fault.
findings.root_cause: Single‑replica entrypoint with no pod disruption budget caused the entire frontend to become unhealthy.
evidence: redis-cart: 1:C 10 Oct 2026 19:31:11.500 # WARNING Memory overcommit must be enabled! Without it, a background save or replication may fail under low memory condition. Being disabled, it can also cause failures without low memory condition, see https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/issues/1328. To fix this issue
findings.fix: Add a second replica to the frontend deployment (frontend-replicas) to provide redundancy and prevent single‑point failure.

findings.title: Cartservice pod kill caused high error rate and outage
findings.what_happened: Killing the only cartservice pod caused error_rate to breach 0.05 and p95 latency to spike to 2900 ms. The service remained unhealthy for 50.583 seconds before recovering.
findings.root_cause: Single‑replica cartservice with no pod disruption budget led to a service outage when the pod was killed.
evidence: frontend: {"error":"could not retrieve cart: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = \"transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 10.96.109.18:7070: connect: connection refused\"","http.req.id":"f4b31b7f-8a3d-44b6-bd5f-5952919ca36e","http.req.method":"GET","http.req.path":"/product/OLJCESP"}
findings.fix: Increase cartservice replicas to 2 (cartservice-replicas) to eliminate single‑point failure.

findings.title: Redis-cart pod kill caused high latency but no data loss
findings.what_happened: Killing the redis-cart pod caused p95 latency to reach 3200 ms, breaching the 1000 ms threshold. No integrity violations were recorded.
findings.root_cause: Redis-cart is a stateful service using an emptyDir volume; pod termination loses in‑memory state and causes latency spikes.
evidence: redis-cart: 1:C 10 Oct 2026 19:31:11.500 * WARNING Memory overcommit must be enabled! Without it, a background save or replication may fail under low memory condition. Being disabled, it can also cause failures without low memory condition, see https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/issues/1328. To fix this issue
findings.fix: Add persistent storage via a PVC (redis-persistence) to preserve cart state across pod restarts and reduce latency.
